evals.prompt:
Render this diagram with beautiful-mermaid as a transparent Tokyo Night SVG and write it to diagram.svg: graph TD
  A[Start] --> B{Ready?}
  B -->|yes| C[Ship]
  B -->|no| D[Fix]
evals.expected_output: A diagram.svg file or SVG block generated with beautiful-mermaid, using the tokyo-night theme and transparent SVG option.
assertions: The output is SVG, not a Mermaid code block or raster image.
The response uses or recommends beautiful-mermaid's renderMermaidSVG API or the bundled render script.
The theme selection is tokyo-night or explicitly equivalent colors.
The output or command includes transparent background handling.

evals.prompt: Add a React component for user-provided Mermaid diagrams using beautiful-mermaid. It should follow our app theme through CSS variables and avoid a render flash.
evals.expected_output: A React component pattern that uses renderMermaidSVG synchronously inside useMemo with CSS variable colors, error handling, and an explicit trust/sanitization boundary for inserted SVG.
assertions: The component imports renderMermaidSVG from beautiful-mermaid.
The component uses useMemo or an equivalent synchronous memoization pattern rather than rendering in useEffect.
The render options pass CSS variable references for bg/fg or related colors.
The component handles parse/render errors instead of crashing silently.
The response explicitly addresses trusted input, sanitization, or an equivalent safety boundary before using dangerouslySetInnerHTML or inserting SVG.

evals.prompt: For a CI comment, convert this Mermaid graph to plain ASCII text with no ANSI escapes: graph LR\n  Build --> Test\n  Test --> Deploy
evals.expected_output: Plain 7-bit ASCII diagram text generated through renderMermaidASCII or the bundled script with colorMode none and useAscii enabled.
assertions: The answer uses beautiful-mermaid's renderMermaidASCII API or the bundled render script.
The response disables ANSI colors with colorMode none or an equivalent option.
The response enables plain 7-bit output with useAscii: true or --use-ascii.
The output is text suitable for logs or Markdown comments and does not rely on Unicode box-drawing characters.
The response does not propose a browser-only SVG renderer as the primary solution.

evals.prompt: Can beautiful-mermaid render a Mermaid gantt chart? If not, what should I do?
evals.expected_output: A boundary-aware answer explaining that beautiful-mermaid supports flowchart/state, sequence, class, ER, and xychart-beta, and suggesting Mermaid CLI or another renderer for Gantt.
assertions: The response does not claim full support for every Mermaid diagram type.
The response lists or references beautiful-mermaid's supported subset.
The response suggests a Mermaid-compatible alternative for Gantt charts.
The response avoids inventing a beautiful-mermaid Gantt API.
